page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs. The hardware allocation includes an exceptionally large memory capacity of 1344.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 84.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and a substantial 260 MB L3 cache.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as Gzip and Bzip3, also perform in the top 25 percent. Multi-core operations, memory bandwidth, and database operations generally align with average mid-tier performance. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which assist in workloads like low-parameter LLM inference where text generation for a 135M model reaches a strong 282.43 tokens per second.

Tradeoffs of this configuration include the complete absence of local storage, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio makes this server highly specialized for memory-intensive workloads that do not scale linearly with core count. It is best suited for large in-memory databases, heavy caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
